lane: B2 — the stink bag is clickable but shows no image on the character sheet
owner_item: "Stink bags — they're clickable now, but you don't have their image. Should be able to see their image on the character sheet."
root_cause:
THE WIRING IS ALREADY THERE AND IS CORRECT END-TO-END. I walked every hop and every one exists in master at 7d1514b: `stinkCloudSheet` emits `portrait: { kind: 'namedBuildingFrame', building: 'stinkBag', recipeId: 'stinkTower' }` (characterSheetModel.ts:1418) → `main.ts:1093-1094` maps `case 'stinkBag': return stinkCloudRenderer.portraitTexture()` → `stinkCloudRenderer.portraitTexture()` (stinkCloudRenderer.ts:93-96) returns idle frame 0 → `drawPortrait`'s texture arm (characterSheet.ts:602-612) draws it. THE ART EXISTS AND IS GOOD: `public/godly/stink-bag/anim/stink-bag-atlas.png` is 1536x128 RGBA (I read the IHDR), exactly 12 cells of 128 as `stink-bag-anim.json` declares, and I measured frame 0 at 38.3% fully-opaque pixels in a clean bbox (8,10)-(116,127), mean RGB (124,103,54) — a real brown sack, not a ghost wash. Both files are `git ls-files`-tracked (exit 0) and present in `dist/`.

SO THE DEFECT IS NOT A MISSING FIX — IT IS THE ONE WINDOW IN WHICH THAT FIX SILENTLY LOSES, AND THE WINDOW IS SELF-INFLICTED. `stinkCloudRenderer` is the ONLY renderer in the set whose atlas load is gated behind a data-dependent early return: `sync()` returns at :132-137 when `world.stinkClouds.size === 0` and only reaches `this.ensureAtlas()` at :138. Its three siblings all fire the load on the third line of `sync`, unconditionally, from the first frame of the match — `stinkTowerRenderer.ts:136`, `voltkinTowerRenderer.ts:470`, `princessRenderer.ts:174`. And `portraitTexture()` does not trigger its own load either. So the 222 KB sheet does not begin fetching until the first bag lands, and a bag lives exactly `STINK_CLOUD_LIFETIME_TICKS = 300` = 5 s (constants.ts:3532). The first bag's card is therefore a cold-fetch race against a 5-second object.

WHAT HE SEES WHEN IT LOSES IS EXACTLY HIS COMPLAINT. A null texture does not draw an empty box: `portraitPlateFor` returns `{ kind: 'emblem', recipeId: 'stinkTower' }` (characterSheetModel.ts:565-572) and `drawPortrait` draws `codexCopyFor('stinkTower').emblem` = `{ kind: 'star', hubType: Square, nodes: 3, nodeType: Circle, radius: 38 }` (codexPresentation.ts:110). A card titled STINK BAG draws the stink TOWER's shape constellation — verbatim his S181 wording "Why is it showing the codex shape structure?" and "those blue squares that have nothing to do".

⚠ I AM BEING EXACT ABOUT THE LIMIT OF THIS: I could not find a line that makes the portrait PERMANENTLY null, and I will not invent one. No renderer runs under vitest and I was forbidden to run the app, so I cannot observe the live card. What I can prove is (a) the chain is complete, (b) the art is shipped and good, (c) this renderer alone defers its load behind a data gate that the project's own `goblinRendererLazyAtlas.test.ts` docblock names as a defect class — "a sheet nobody fetches is a permanent green puppet, which is strictly worse than the slow load it replaced" — and (d) the visible symptom of a null is precisely what he described. The fix below closes the window regardless of which frame of it he hit, and costs nothing.

AND THE REASON NOBODY CAUGHT IT IS THE S182 PATTERN, CONFIRMED: the only test that mentions the bag portrait (characterSheetPlate.test.ts:271-282) HAND-WRITES the spec literal and asserts the pure `portraitPlateFor`. Nothing asserts that `stinkCloudSheet` emits that spec, nothing asserts main.ts's switch arm, and nothing asserts the shipped sheet matches its manifest. A guard that proves the shape exists, over a path nothing proves is reached.

evidence.why_it_matters: THE ROOT CAUSE. `ensureAtlas()` sits at :138, BELOW the early return at :132-137. The bag sheet does not begin loading until the first bag exists in the world — unlike every sibling renderer. This is the whole window in which the card can resolve to null.

The sibling contract, unconditional on the third line of sync. voltkinTowerRenderer.ts:470 and princessRenderer.ts:174 are identical in shape. stinkCloudRenderer is the only one of the four that defers its load behind a data condition — that asymmetry IS the finding.

The accessor reads `this.frames` and NEVER calls `ensureAtlas()` itself. A card opening is not an event that can start the load, so the card can only ever wait on the board. Its own docblock at :89 concedes 'NULL UNTIL THE LAZY FETCH LANDS, which is not a defect' — correct in principle, but only because the load was assumed to start early, which here it does not.

The producer side of the S182 fix is present and correct in master. Reconciling the two files the brief named: stinkCloudRenderer.ts:78-83's docblock and this line are the SAME landed fix, not a fix and a stale note. Nothing here needs changing.

The middle hop exists, inside an exhaustive switch with a `never` arm. The instance is the same one synced at main.ts:4052 and constructed at main.ts:864. There is no second StinkCloudRenderer and no second setPortraitSource call (only main.ts:1061), so nothing overwrites this.
ANSWERS 'WHAT IS HE ACTUALLY SEEING' (brief item 2 and 5). A null texture does NOT draw nothing and does NOT draw a broken-texture box. It falls to the emblem arm, because `recipeId` is 'stinkTower'.

fix_shape:
ZERO ART COST. Two changes, both in one production file, plus one new test file.

**(1) Make the sheet's load unreachable-proof — `src/render/stinkCloudRenderer.ts`, two lines.**
- Move `this.ensureAtlas();` from :138 to immediately after `this.haze.clear();` at :131, i.e. ABOVE the `world.stinkClouds.size === 0` early return. This makes it byte-identical in shape to `stinkTowerRenderer.ts:136` / `voltkinTowerRenderer.ts:470` / `princessRenderer.ts:174`. Cost: one 222 KB fetch per match that today happens a few seconds later anyway. That is 0.2% of the 105.8 MiB static payload and it is the same sheet the board will need.
- ALSO call `this.ensureAtlas();` as the first line of `portraitTexture()` (:93). This is the belt-and-braces half and it is what makes the card self-sufficient: opening a card becomes an event that can start the load, so the portrait can never be the thing waiting on the board. ⚠ State in the docblock that `towerRenderer.portraitTexture` (towerRenderer.ts:398) does NOT self-trigger — this branch is deliberately going further than that sibling, not accidentally diverging from it. Do NOT change towerRenderer; that is another lane's file.
- Update the `⚠ NULL UNTIL THE LAZY FETCH LANDS` docblock at :89-91 so the next session does not re-derive the old reasoning: the null window is now bounded by one fetch started at the card's own open, not by whether a bag has ever landed.

**(2) Close the S182 hole with tests that are mechanical, not prose — NEW FILE `src/render/stinkBagPortrait.test.ts`.** Three assertions, none of which needs a renderer or a DOM:
- **The producer.** Build a real `World` with one `makeStinkCloud` (copy the fixture shape from `characterSheetMirror.test.ts:89-99`, which already does exactly this), call `characterSheetModel(world, seat, { kind: 'stinkCloud', id })`, and assert `view.portrait` deep-equals `{ kind: 'namedBuildingFrame', building: 'stinkBag', recipeId: 'stinkTower' }`. THIS IS THE ASSERTION THAT DOES NOT EXIST TODAY — `characterSheetPlate.test.ts:271` hand-writes the literal precisely because it did not want to build a world.
- **The shipped sheet, read off disk.** Copy `voltkinAtlas.test.ts`'s pattern (`readFileSync('public/godly/voltkin/anim/voltkin-anim.json')`): parse `stink-bag-anim.json`, assert `states.idle` exists with `row: 0`, then read the PNG's IHDR (bytes 16..24, big-endian) and assert `width === cellW * idle.frames` and `height >= (idle.row + 1) * cellH`. No numpy, no Pillow, no `check:atlas` lane — pure `node:fs` + `Buffer.readUInt32BE`, so it runs in the normal vitest suite. This is the guard that would catch a re-packed or half-copied sheet, which is the one failure mode that WOULD make the portrait permanently null.
- **The wiring arm, enumerated mechanically rather than asserted by substring.** Read `src/main.ts` as text, isolate the `switch (spec.building)` block, count its `case '` arms, pin the total at 3, and assert the set is exactly `{stinkTower, stinkBag, voltkin}` with three DISTINCT renderer accessors on the right-hand sides. ⛔ STATE ITS LIMIT IN THE DOCBLOCK, per the S182 rule: this proves the arm EXISTS and that no two buildings share a renderer (the bug the S182 self-audit note at main.ts:1085-1090 describes); it CANNOT prove the arm is reached. The producer assertion above is what covers reachability on the model side, and nothing in vitest can cover the Pixi side. Say so plainly.
- ⚠ CRLF: this file parses a repo source file, so match `\r?\n` in any regex — a `ci.*.test.ts` that does not false-reds on Windows only while CI stays green (memory: ci-source-text-guards-need-crlf-normalisation).

**WHAT NOT TO DO.**
- Do NOT touch `src/render/characterSheetPlate.test.ts`. Its existing bag test is correct as far as it goes and it is a wide sweep file other lanes may be in.
- Do NOT touch `src/main.ts`. The new guard READS it; nothing in it needs editing.
- Do NOT change the emblem fallback. If the owner would rather see a word plate than the tower's star during a load window, that is his call — but with the fix above the window is one fetch long and the question is moot. Ask only if he raises it.
- Do NOT widen `BAG_PICK_R` (controls.ts:233 = 26). Observation only, NOT this branch's scope: the drawn bag is 128 x SPRITE_SCALE 0.34 ≈ 43 px tall anchored at the feet (`footAnchor.y` 0.9922), so a 26 px disc about `bag.pos` covers roughly the bottom two-thirds of the art plus 26 px of bare ground below it — the same "Vlad's knees" geometry S181 fixed for creatures. He said the bag IS clickable, so this is his to raise, not ours to change.

art_cost:
NO-ART — and this is the single most valuable finding in the lane, established definitively rather than assumed.

The bag art ALREADY SHIPS and is ALREADY the thing the accessor returns. `public/godly/stink-bag/anim/stink-bag-atlas.png` is 1536x128 RGBA (dimensions read from the PNG IHDR, not guessed) = exactly the 12 cells of 128 that `stink-bag-anim.json` declares for `states.idle` at row 0. I measured every cell: frame 0 is 38.3% fully-opaque (alpha 255) with a clean solid bbox of (8,10)-(116,127) and mean solid RGB (124,103,54) — a brown sack filling the cell, with 50.6% of the cell at alpha 0 and only 2.6% in the 1-31 ghost-wash band, i.e. it does NOT have the translucent-box defect the S183 sheets needed cleaning for. Both files are tracked (`git ls-files --error-unmatch` exit 0) and present in `dist/`, and `public/**` is in deploy.yml's paths filter so they ship.

Belt and braces beyond that, all free:
- `assets-source/stink-bag/` holds the full source kit — `stink-bag-still.png` (281 KB hi-res), four rejected landed stills, `atlas-spec.json`, `clip-spec.json` and the chosen clip. If a crop ever needs redoing it can be repacked with `node scripts/build-sprite-atlas.mjs assets-source/stink-bag/atlas-spec.json`. ⚠ `assets-source/` is NOT served at runtime (only `public/` is copied by Vite), so the still cannot be a runtime fallback — it is a re-pack source only.

So brief item 4's "draw the same procedural bag into the portrait" is not on the table — but it is not needed, because the sprite path is the cheap path and it is already built.

⛔ NOTHING IN THIS LANE SHOULD REACH FOR veo, imagen, or any generator. Not one pixel. If a future session is tempted, the correct move is `scripts/build-sprite-atlas.mjs` against the existing `assets-source/stink-bag/clips/`, which costs nothing.

WHAT THE NEW TESTS DO PIN (all in `src/render/stinkBagPortrait.test.ts`, all pure / node:fs, no DOM):
1. **The producer, which nothing pins today.** `characterSheetModel(world, seat, {kind:'stinkCloud', id})` on a real world with one `makeStinkCloud` must return `portrait` deep-equal to `{kind:'namedBuildingFrame', building:'stinkBag', recipeId:'stinkTower'}`. 2. **The shipped sheet against its manifest, read off disk** — `states.idle.row === 0`, `PNG width === cellW * idle.frames` (1536), `PNG height >= cellH`. IHDR bytes only, so no numpy/Pillow and no dependence on the `atlas-guard` CI job. This is REAL coverage of the one failure mode that would make the portrait permanently null.
3. **The main.ts arm, enumerated.** Count the `case '` arms in the `switch (spec.building)` block, pin at 3, assert the three building literals and three DISTINCT accessors.

STATED LIMITS, which must go in the file's docblock verbatim so the next session inherits them and not a false sense of cover:
- Test 3 is a source-text guard. Per S182 it proves the line EXISTS; it cannot prove the line is REACHED. It is mechanical (a count, not a substring) so a fourth building fails it, but it is not reachability.
- NOTHING here pins `drawPortrait` actually blitting the texture, the sprite's scale/position inside the 76px box (`PORTRAIT = 76`, characterSheet.ts:51), or the atlas fetch succeeding in a browser. Those are Playwright-or-nothing, and the only honest check available today is the owner clicking a bag.

If the branch wants the ordering pinned, the ONLY cheap option is a source-text assertion that `ensureAtlas()` appears in `sync` BEFORE the `stinkClouds.size === 0` guard — worth doing, and worth labelling as the weak guard it is.
- OPTIONAL, only if the branch has room: a `@races`-lane Playwright observation would be the one thing that could see the card. It is NOT recommended here — each observation costs ~30 s of SIM time, the lane exists for castle/backdrop work, and a stink tower has to be built and fire first. Say "not attempted, and why" rather than silently omitting it.
